canonical_statement: If $\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$ then let\[f(n)=\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\tau(2^k-1).\]Does $f(2n)/f(n)$ tend to a limit?

must_determine: Unfolded: for every R∈ℝ there exists N such that for every n≥N the ratio is at least R, with the exact frozen f and division conventions.
close_branch_A.statement: AFFIRMATIVE CLOSE: prove the ratio f(2n)/f(n) tends to +∞ on the full natural tail.

must_determine: Give a real R such that for every N there exists n≥N with f(2n)/f(n)<R (or an exactly equivalent not-Tendsto witness). Mere unboundedness is compatible with Branch A and cannot serve as Branch B.
close_branch_B.statement: NEGATIVE CLOSE: prove the literal failure of Tendsto to +∞ for the exact ratio.

definitions:
Formal-semantics guard: for this frozen source record the current Lean target signature is exactly `theorem erdos_893 :

Quantifier-order guard: preserve every explicit and implicit universal/existential quantifier exactly as stated; no finite checking or selected parameter family may substitute for the stated scope.

Limit guard: every lim/limsup/liminf statement is along the full directed sequence specified by the source (normally the natural variable tending to infinity), not merely along a favorable subsequence. A finite limit is distinct from divergence to infinity and from bounded limsup.

The controlling open target is the frozen Lean proposition Tendsto (fun n ↦ f(2*n)/f(n)) atTop atTop, i.e. the ratio tends to +∞. The prose phrase 'tend to a limit' is broader and is not controlling: published unboundedness already excludes a finite limit but does not prove divergence to +∞.
The three logical possibilities finite-limit, divergence to +∞, and neither are kept distinct. The source's solved unboundedness theorem is permitted background only as unboundedness.
invariants_that_must_survive_every_refor: The canonical statement text is immutable; every proof target must imply exactly that statement (or its literal negation for a negative close).
Every quantifier, domain, hypothesis, strict/non-strict inequality, endpoint, normalization, and parameter dependency survives every reformulation.
Discrete structure is preserved: integrality, distinctness, ordering, multiplicity/set-vs-multiset conventions, and exact cardinalities may not be relaxed silently.

The frozen current Lean signature remains semantically consistent with the prose contract; binder types and predicates may not be altered merely to make the theorem easier to prove.
The answer wrapper is fixed to the truth of the +∞ Tendsto proposition; f uses the exact frozen divisor-counting σ0/τ convention and interval endpoints.
known_traps: QUANTIFIER SLIP: exchanging ∀ and ∃, moving an epsilon/constant after the limiting variable, or replacing “all sufficiently large” by “infinitely many”.
SAMPLED-TO-UNIVERSAL: checking many finite instances and promoting the observation to an unrestricted theorem without a valid finite-reduction theorem.
DOMAIN DRIFT: proving a translated/scaled/relaxed version without an exact map back to the original domain, endpoints, and discrete constraints.
STRENGTH CONFUSION: refuting a stronger folklore conjecture does not refute the canonical claim; proving a weaker statement does not prove it.

FORMAL/PROSE DRIFT: a Lean proof is acceptable only if the exact frozen signature is semantically the same target. `answer(sorry)` or independently filled answer metavariables are not permission to choose an easier proposition/function.
UNBOUNDED-VS-DIVERGENT: limsup=∞ or unbounded range does not imply eventual exceedance of every threshold.
PROSE LIMIT: the known absence of a finite limit does not settle the +∞ target.
non_results: A theorem for only a selected finite set of parameter values when the statement is uniform or asymptotic.
A result only on a favorable subsequence, density-one subset, almost-everywhere set, or “generic” family when the canonical statement requires the full sequence/all objects.
A numerical fit, heuristic, Monte Carlo result, floating-point experiment, or finite computation without a proved finite-reduction/transfer theorem to the canonical claim.

A conditional theorem whose decisive premise is an unproved conjecture of comparable strength.
A reduction to an equivalent-strength open problem, a tautological rephrasing, or a definition of the requested answer in terms of the original target predicate.
A continuous/real-valued/LP/SDP relaxation without a proved integrality or exact-transfer theorem when the canonical objects are discrete.
A stronger-looking statement in a different normalization/domain that does not formally imply the canonical statement.
Convergence of f(2n)/f(n) to any finite real value does not establish the frozen formal target Tendsto (fun n ↦ f(2*n)/f(n)) atTop atTop; the controlling machine target asks divergence to +∞.
Reproving only unboundedness of the ratio does not establish convergence to +∞ on the full sequence.
The published/source unboundedness sibling alone is not a close of Tendsto atTop atTop.
